statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any published hour and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor.
recommendation: Tail holds a closed-venue floor of 4-5% across all 24 published hours, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout. Stress drifts from 41% to 50%, entering the elevated band from 18:00 UTC on 5 September, reflecting hawkish September rate pricing after Friday's payroll beat and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium carried unpriced across the halt. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt, with the whole 24-hour horizon ending about ten hours before the Sunday restart, so Tail holds a closed-venue floor while hawkish September rate pricing and a Hormuz energy premium accumulate unpriced
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions during that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. The Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation release shows August nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against a consensus near 56,000, the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% on the year. Reuters reported the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting rising to 58.4% from 49.4% the previous day, while the H.15 release carries the two-year Treasury yield at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77%. The VIX settled at 14.53, up 1.47% from 14.32 and still a low absolute base. Broad indices closed lower even as the Nasdaq-100 held a small gain, with the S&P 500 down 0.38% and the Dow down 0.51%, a narrow and internally mixed signature rather than the aligned cross-asset stack a genuine tail regime requires. Energy remains the principal unresolved input: WTI settled at $91.48 after a weekly advance near 10% and Brent at $92.68 after a 7.6% week, driven by renewed US-Iran strikes and continued impairment of Strait of Hormuz shipping, with average US diesel at a record $5.85 per gallon. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the 21:00 UTC Friday settle and reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, roughly ten hours after the last hour published here. No forecast hour in this assessment can therefore contain an observable price path, and Tail is scored at a closed-venue floor throughout rather than from any directional view. Stress carries the accumulating weight of a hawkish September rate path, an energy-supply premium feeding the inflation outlook, an unresolved military exchange with an open weekend headline window, and a data-heavy week ahead containing August PPI on 10 September and August CPI on 11 September. The first genuine price-path evaluation of the new week belongs to a later assessment run after the Globex restart.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the closing two thirds of the August payroll session and the first seventeen hours of the CME weekend halt. The 13:00 UTC hour on 4 September still carried the release aftermath at Tail 20% and Stress 64% under an event/whipsaw mode, the only WATCH hour in the window. Tail then decayed steadily through the US cash session as the index retraced its highs and recovered, with mode moving to mixed from 15:00 UTC as semiconductor leadership diverged from a softer broad tape, reaching Tail 12% and Stress 48% by 20:00 UTC. From the 21:00 UTC futures settlement onward every hour has been scored at the closed-venue floor of Tail 5% with Stress at 38-40% and mode normal. All 24 slots carry a published Claude assessment.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 41% to 50%, entering the elevated band from 18:00 UTC on 5 September, reflecting hawkish September rate pricing after Friday's payroll beat, an energy premium from continued Strait of Hormuz disruption, and an open two-sided weekend headline window. Confidence eases from 85% to 78% purely through the ageing of Friday-anchored evidence and stays inside the high band because the evidence set remains complete. The horizon ends at 12:00 UTC on 6 September, roughly ten hours before the scheduled 22:00 UTC Globex restart, so the first live price-path evaluation belongs to a later run.
